noteRef.topicTitle: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

specPoints.text: understand the reactions of alkanes with: i oxygen in the air (combustion) ii halogens
know the general formula of alkanes and cycloalkanes, and understand that they are hydrocarbons (compounds of carbon and hydrogen only) which are saturated (contain single bonds only)

primer.text: Alkanes are the quiet members of the hydrocarbon family: saturated, near non-polar and reluctant to react. This note counts the first six members, states the general formula, then wakes them up with two reactions that matter - complete and incomplete combustion, whose products differ only in how much oxygen the flame can breathe.

lessons.title: The alkane family and its low reactivity
sourceHeadings: The First Six Members of the Alkane Family
lessons.opening: Alkanes are the saturated baseline of organic chemistry: carbon and hydrogen only, single bonds throughout, and a general formula every member obeys. Their reluctance to react is not laziness but structure - strong, non-polar bonds with nothing for attackers to grip.
keyPoints: Open-chain alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2.
The first six members are methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane and hexane.
Saturated means every bond is single, with the maximum hydrogen count the carbons can hold.
Cycloalkanes close a ring and therefore drop two hydrogens, following CnH2n.
Strong carbon-hydrogen bonds and near-zero polarity make alkanes famously unreactive.

low.restatement: Alkanes carry only single bonds and follow CnH2n+2 open-chain or CnH2n ring-closed; their strong, even-handed bonds leave attackers little to grip.
low.analogy: A saturated chain is a fully occupied car park - no spaces (unsaturated sites) for new arrivals to enter.
low.examPointer: Do not forget the +2 in CnH2n+2 - quoting the alkene formula for alkanes is the single most common formula slip.

medium.restatement: Reactivity tracks polarisation and bond strength: C-H bonds are strong and their electrons are shared almost evenly, so alkanes resist both electrophiles and nucleophiles and react only with oxygen, halogens under light, or under cracking conditions.
medium.analogy: An uncharged, well-built lock resists both magnets and crowbars - only the right key (oxygen, light-activated halogen) engages it.
medium.examPointer: When a question asks why alkanes are unreactive, give both reasons: bond strength and lack of polarity - one reason alone is half an answer.

check.stem: Which formula is the general formula of an open-chain alkane?

options.explanation: Saturated chains carry the maximum hydrogen count.
That belongs to alkenes and cycloalkanes.
That belongs to species with two degrees of unsaturation.
That is the alkanol (alcohol) series.

check.stem: What does saturated mean for a hydrocarbon?

options.text: Only single bonds, holding the maximum possible hydrogen
options.explanation: No double bond remains to open.

options.text: The molecule contains the most carbons possible
options.explanation: Saturation is about bonds and hydrogens, not size.
Saturation has a solution meaning too - not this one.
Alkanes are neutral molecules.

check.stem: Which hydrocarbon is a cycloalkane?

options.explanation: The closed ring costs two hydrogens versus hexane's C6H14.
That is the open-chain member.
That is an alkene, not a cycloalkane.
That carries a double bond - a cycloalkene.

check.stem: Why are alkanes so unreactive toward most reagents?

options.text: Their C-H bonds are strong and the electrons are shared almost evenly
options.explanation: Neither electrophiles nor nucleophiles find a grip.

options.text: Their bonds are weak and polar
options.explanation: Weak polar bonds are the reactive case, not alkanes.
Alkanes are covalent molecules.
Alkanes are hydrocarbons - no oxygen present.

check.stem: How does the molar mass progress from methane to ethane to propane?

options.explanation: CH4 is 16; each CH2 step adds 14.

options.text: Up 14 each time including into methane
options.explanation: Methane to ethane adds CH2 plus the initial carbon's two extra hydrogens - 16 then 14 thereafter.
That counts carbon only.
Members differ in composition.

check.stem: State the general formula of open-chain alkanes and list the first six members by name.
check.modelAnswer: CnH2n+2; methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane, hexane.

check.stem: Explain, in two sentences, why cycloalkanes carry two fewer hydrogens than their open-chain equivalents.
check.modelAnswer: Closing a carbon ring uses two bonding positions that open-chain members spend on hydrogen; cyclohexane therefore holds C6H12 where hexane holds C6H14.

check.stem: Explain why alkane molecules show essentially no polarity.
check.modelAnswer: Carbon and hydrogen have nearly matching electronegativities, so every C-H bond shares its pair almost evenly and the dipoles cancel across the symmetric molecule.

check.stem: A hydrocarbon has formula C5H12. Classify it as alkane, cycloalkane or alkene and justify using the formulas.
check.modelAnswer: C5H12 fits CnH2n+2, so it is an open-chain alkane - pentane; a cycloalkane of five carbons would be C5H10 and an alkene likewise C5H10.

lessons.title: Complete combustion: the fuel reaction
lessons.opening: Given plenty of oxygen, alkanes burn to carbon dioxide and water, releasing the heat that makes them fuels. Balancing the equations is the skill: oxygen's count must cover both the carbon dioxide and the water produced.
keyPoints: Complete combustion needs plentiful oxygen and produces only carbon dioxide and water.
Methane burns as CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, releasing heat energy.
Propane burns as C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O - oxygen must serve both products.
The near-zero polarity of alkane bonds does not stop combustion; oxygen attacks the C-H and C-C bonds energetically.
Exothermic heat release is why alkanes power engines and heating systems.

low.restatement: With enough air, the alkane's carbon all becomes carbon dioxide and its hydrogen all becomes water - balance the oxygen last.
low.analogy: Complete combustion is a clean ledger: every carbon pays into CO2, every hydrogen into H2O, and oxygen balances the books.
low.examPointer: Balance water before oxygen: set CO2 from carbons, H2O from hydrogens, then divide the total oxygen demand across the O2 coefficient.

medium.restatement: The oxidation is strongly exothermic because the new C=O and O-H bonds formed outweigh the C-H and C-C bonds broken; oxygen's abundance is what keeps the ledger on the complete side.
medium.analogy: The bond account swaps cheap holdings (C-H, C-C) for premium ones (C=O, O-H) and pays out the difference as heat.
medium.examPointer: Write state symbols when asked for full equations - gaseous fuels, gaseous CO2, liquid or gaseous water as the question specifies.

check.stem: What are the two products of complete alkane combustion?

options.explanation: Plentiful oxygen drives both products out fully.
Carbon monoxide marks incomplete combustion.
That is the soot case of limited oxygen.
Hydrogen does not appear as a combustion product.

check.stem: Which coefficient balances the oxygen in the propane combustion equation?

options.explanation: C3H8 + 5O2 -> 3CO2 + 4H2O: oxygen atoms 10 = 6 + 4.
That leaves the oxygen ledger one atom short.
That overcounts the oxygen demand.
That covers only the carbon dioxide.

check.stem: Why do alkane bonds' low polarity not prevent combustion?

options.text: Combustion is driven by the much stronger bonds formed in the products
options.explanation: The energy payoff outweighs the reluctance of the starting bonds.

options.text: Oxygen is non-polar too, so polarity never matters
options.explanation: The product bond strengths, not matching polarity, drive the reaction.
The reaction remains covalent bond reshuffling.
Combustion plainly occurs.

check.stem: Which statement about methane's combustion equation is correct?

options.text: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O is balanced on every element

options.explanation: The oxygen ledger gives 2 versus 4 - short by two.
Hydrogen shows 4 versus 2.
Hydrogen shows 8 versus 4.

check.stem: Why are alkanes prized as fuels?

options.text: Their complete combustion is strongly exothermic
options.explanation: The heat released powers engines and heating.
Combustion releases energy - the opposite.
Price is not the chemistry answer sought.

options.text: They produce oxygen as they burn
options.explanation: They consume oxygen.

check.stem: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of methane.
State the products and the condition required for complete combustion of any alkane.
check.modelAnswer: Plentiful oxygen as the condition; carbon dioxide and water as the only products.

check.stem: Explain why a limited oxygen supply changes the products of alkane combustion.
check.modelAnswer: With too little oxygen the carbon cannot all reach the +4 oxidation state of carbon dioxide, so carbon monoxide or even soot forms instead, and less heat is released.

check.stem: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of butane, C4H10.
check.modelAnswer: 2C4H10 + 13O2 -> 8CO2 + 10H2O: carbons 8=8, hydrogens 20=20, and the 26 oxygen atoms supplied by 13 O2 divide as 16 into the eight CO2 and 10 into the ten H2O.

lessons.title: Incomplete combustion and the halogen door
lessons.opening: Starve the flame of oxygen and the products turn toxic: carbon monoxide replaces carbon dioxide and soot may follow. Open a different door - halogen molecules under ultraviolet light - and alkanes substitute hydrogen for halogen in the radical chemistry the next note develops.
keyPoints: Incomplete combustion occurs when oxygen is limited, producing carbon monoxide and sometimes soot.
Carbon monoxide is a colourless, odourless, highly toxic gas.
The limited-oxygen route releases less energy than complete combustion.
Alkanes react with halogens under ultraviolet light by free-radical substitution.
The substitution swaps one halogen atom for one hydrogen on the chain, one at a time.

low.restatement: Not enough oxygen means carbon monoxide (and soot) instead of carbon dioxide, less heat, and a silent poisoning risk; halogens plus UV light swap onto the chain one atom at a time.
low.analogy: A starving fire eats what it can reach - CO is the half-digested carbon that never finished its meal.
low.examPointer: Pair the product with its condition: CO means limited oxygen; CO2 means plentiful oxygen. Condition-product matching carries the mark.

medium.restatement: Energetics and kinetics separate the two halogen behaviours: without light the halogen molecule meets an unreactive alkane and nothing happens, but UV splits the halogen homolytically into radicals that can extract hydrogen from the strong C-H bonds.
medium.analogy: The alkane is a vault that only light can open for the halogen: darkness keeps the door shut, UV hands the halogen radical keys.
medium.examPointer: Mention the UV requirement explicitly in halogen questions - omitting the condition loses the mark even with a correct equation.

check.stem: Which product of incomplete alkane combustion is the toxic one?

options.explanation: Limited oxygen leaves carbon half-oxidised as the silent poison.
CO2 is the complete-combustion product and not acutely toxic in this context.
Water is harmless.
Nitrogen passes through air unchanged.

check.stem: What condition must accompany a halogen for alkane substitution to proceed?

options.explanation: UV homolytically splits the halogen molecule into radicals.
Nickel belongs to alkene hydrogenation.
Acid catalysts serve alkene hydration.
Darkness actually prevents the radical route.

check.stem: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous in homes?

options.text: It is colourless and odourless while binding strongly where oxygen should
options.explanation: The gas poisons silently.
Soot stains; CO is invisible and leaves no stain.
CO is flammable but the danger cited is toxicity.
CO has no smell at all.

check.stem: What type of reaction occurs between methane and chlorine in sunlight?

options.explanation: Radicals swap a chlorine onto the chain, releasing HCl.
Addition needs a pi bond - alkanes have none.
No acid-base pair operates.
That is analytical chemistry, not this reaction.

check.stem: Which equation represents the incomplete combustion of methane?

options.explanation: Carbon monoxide replaces carbon dioxide under the limited supply.
That is the complete route.
That is decomposition, not combustion.
Hydrogen gas is not a combustion product.

check.stem: State the products of incomplete combustion of an alkane when oxygen is very limited.
check.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide and water, with soot (carbon) also appearing under extreme limitation.

check.stem: Name the reaction type and condition for methane reacting with bromine.
check.modelAnswer: Free-radical substitution, requiring ultraviolet light to start the radical chain.

check.stem: Explain why incomplete combustion releases less energy than complete combustion.
check.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide still stores usable oxidation energy that complete combustion would have released, so the limited-oxygen route pays out a smaller energy dividend.

check.stem: A faulty boiler burns methane with a restricted air supply. Name the hazard gas and write its balanced formation equation within the combustion.
check.modelAnswer: The hazard is carbon monoxide; within the combustion ledger, methane burning incompletely forms it as 2CH4 + 3O2 -> 2CO + 4H2O.

glossary.definition: Describing a hydrocarbon holding only single bonds and the maximum hydrogen count.
Burning with plentiful oxygen to give only carbon dioxide and water.
The toxic, colourless, odourless product of incomplete combustion.
The UV-initiated reaction swapping a halogen atom onto an alkane chain via radicals.
